summary: Install- and import-time beacon posts host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: @ppa-web-components/ppa-banner@1.0.0 ships no functional component code: index.js exports a Proxy whose every property is a no-op stub. The package's actual behavior is a reconnaissance beacon in beacon.cjs, which is wired to run both via package.json's postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and from the main entry on require(). The beacon collects host identifiers — os.hostname(), the install path, process.cwd(), and process.version — and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded plaintext HTTP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The scoped name, the no-op Proxy export, and the install- and import-time callback together are consistent with dependency-confusion or namespace-hijack reconnaissance scaffolding targeting an internal `@ppa-web-components/*` namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
